prompt_text:
You are extending one independently audited open-problem draft in a sealed paired experiment.

Read only source /evidence/source.json, parent /evidence/parent.json, and independent audit /evidence/audit.json. Do not use the web, any prior-run file other than those exact sealed inputs, any other solution, or any verification report. You may create exact-arithmetic checks only under /work; do not modify files outside /work.

Parent SHA-256: 792af91d188a0bdf024c5c3d04409e91f6dc61d96b6e7498a2ef4183ae44c11a
Audit SHA-256: 9797ca96e4620fe52b31e8f64a67a9d912add7302dfa752d65642e3f44ae943a

This is an exact-closure attempt after the three scheduled search lenses. Concentrate on resolving the independent audit. If no material proof change is required, copy claimed_resolution, every claim and proof_sketch, and final_writeup from the parent exactly.

Address every REFUTED or UNRESOLVED claim and the audit's target-coverage judgment. Preserve correct progress. Repair, narrow, replace, or remove unsupported claims. Never call the open target solved without a complete proof at the requested strength. Put every load-bearing claim in a separate results item in proof order. There is no claim-count cap. The entire ordered proof is in scope. Keep final_writeup under 3,000 words and each proof_sketch under 500 words.

Complete independent audit:
--- BEGIN AUDIT ---
{
  "record_id": "tcs_count_graphs_vc_at_most_k",
  "stage": "REVISION_AUDIT",
  "arm": "plain",
  "iteration": 4,
  "parent_sha256": "792af91d188a0bdf024c5c3d04409e91f6dc61d96b6e7498a2ef4183ae44c11a",
  "complete": true,
  "claims": [
    {
      "idx": 0,
      "claim": "Complement equivalence and exact endpoint cases. Let F(n,k) count labelled graphs on [n] with vertex-cover number at most k, let N=binom(n,2), and put m=n−k. For 0≤k≤n, F(n,k)=2^N−T(n,m), where T(n,m) is the number of labelled K_m-free graphs. Consequently F(n,n−3)=2^N−T(n,3), with T(n,3) the triangle-free graph count. Also F(n,0)=1; F(n,1)=1+n(2^{n−1}−1)−binom(n,2); F(n,n−2)=2^N−1; and F(n,n−1)=F(n,n)=2^N.",
      "claim_sha256": "9f87e08e596020b4fd50076061156f82599554e1b6b984faffd52442ade03500",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "For every graph, τ(G)=n−α(G), and complementation bijects graphs having an independent m-set with graphs containing K_m. The endpoint formulas follow directly; for k=1, nonempty star subgraphs are uniquely centered except that each one-edge graph is counted twice. Exact enumeration through n=6 confirmed all applicable identities.",
      "witness": "none",
      "search_method": "Independent bijective proof and exhaustive exact-integer enumeration; no web or unapproved evidence.",
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_v2_fixed_point_extension_v3_scratch/tcs_count_graphs_vc_at_most_k/audit/plain/attempt_4/audit_attempt4_checker.py"
    },
    {
      "idx": 1,
      "claim": "Two-sided family-size lower bounds. For 2≤m≤n, put r=m−1, write n=ar+s with 0≤s<r, and let e(n,m)=[n²−s(a+1)²−(r−s)a²]/2. Then T(n,m)≥2^{e(n,m)} and F(n,n−m)≥2^{N−binom(m,2)}. For fixed m≥3, e(n,m)=(m−2)n²/[2(m−1)]+O_m(1); specifically e(n,3)=floor(n²/4).",
      "claim_sha256": "9014e08b9852ad0648fbaa0edde99338f25f51fe37f58f8a5ff4c7c47a27151a",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "All subgraphs of a fixed balanced complete (m−1)-partite graph are K_m-free, giving exactly 2^e graphs. Forcing the edges inside one fixed m-set to be absent gives 2^{N−binom(m,2)} graphs counted by F. Algebra gives e=(m−2)n²/[2(m−1)]−s(m−1−s)/[2(m−1)], proving the stated asymptotic and triangle case.",
      "witness": "none",
      "search_method": "Independent extremal construction and exact algebra, supplemented by exhaustive small-order checks.",
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_v2_fixed_point_extension_v3_scratch/tcs_count_graphs_vc_at_most_k/audit/plain/attempt_4/audit_attempt4_checker.py"
    },
    {
      "idx": 2,
      "claim": "Enumeration-strategy obstruction and its sharp endpoint boundary. For every fixed m≥3, both F(n,n−m) and T(n,m) have 2^{Θ(n²)} members. More generally, if m≥3 and k=n−m≥cn for a constant c>0, both families have 2^{Ω(n²)} members. Thus an algorithm that explicitly lists every admissible graph, or instead every K_m-free graph before subtracting from 2^N, cannot run in 2^{o(n²)} time in this regime. At m=2, T(n,2)=1, whereas at m=3 already T(n,3)≥2^{floor(n²/4)}; hence k=n−3 is the first fixed-distance-from-n endpoint where neither side can be explicitly enumerated within the target time. This does not prove a lower bound against implicit exact counting.",
      "claim_sha256": "f49d6f0beeede0323cb4a7a43ec3ec7571c57bac2d2abb2b81f52656d07714aa",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "Claim 1 and the 2^N upper bound prove the fixed-m statement. In the general regime, q=k(2n−k−1)/2≥k(n−1)/2=Ω(n²), while every subgraph of a balanced complete bipartite graph is K_m-free for m≥3. Explicit listing therefore needs at least one operation per family member. K_2-free graphs consist only of the edgeless graph, whereas the m=3 lower bound is quadratic-exponential. The draft correctly limits this obstruction to explicit enumeration.",
      "witness": "none",
      "search_method": "Manual asymptotic and computational-model analysis, with exact finite checks of the underlying bounds.",
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_v2_fixed_point_extension_v3_scratch/tcs_count_graphs_vc_at_most_k/audit/plain/attempt_4/audit_attempt4_checker.py"
    },
    {
      "idx": 3,
      "claim": "There is a deterministic exact algorithm using polynomial space and time 2^{q+O(n)}, where q=binom(n,2)−binom(n−k,2)=kn−k(k+1)/2. Therefore the target is achieved whenever k=o(n), including k=O(n/log n).",
      "claim_sha256": "228df9eb30a58bc730a1e71110147b812d8099ebb8fb314e52a76c0c9cfea95e",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "For each k-set C there are exactly 2^q graphs with no edge outside C. Retaining a generated graph only for its first k-cover counts every graph with τ≤k exactly once, since any smaller cover extends to a k-cover. At most binom(n,k)^2 polynomial-time tests per generated edge pattern give 2^{q+O(n)} time, and enumeration plus an O(n²)-bit counter uses polynomial space. Since q≤nk, k=o(n) gives q=o(n²).",
      "witness": "none",
      "search_method": "Direct algorithm reconstruction and worst-case runtime/space accounting; exact q identities were checked computationally.",
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_v2_fixed_point_extension_v3_scratch/tcs_count_graphs_vc_at_most_k/audit/plain/attempt_4/audit_attempt4_checker.py"
    },
    {
      "idx": 4,
      "claim": "Structural hard-strip reduction. For n≥2 let ℓ(n)=floor(n/ceil(log₂n)). A deterministic exact 2^{o(n²)}-time algorithm for every 0≤k≤n exists if and only if one exists uniformly on the restricted strip ℓ(n)<k≤n−3. Equivalently, under m=n−k, the only unresolved range needed for the full target is 3≤m≤n−ℓ(n)−1.",
      "claim_sha256": "175fcbd3c3b79901b71b76aa8cb480a5fac80c3be6c509f9c0dd8a6ac533d2dd",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "Restriction proves the forward implication. Conversely, k≤ℓ(n) is handled by Claim 3 with q≤n²/ceil(log₂n)=o(n²), k≥n−2 by the endpoint formulas, and every remaining integer lies in the stated strip. Substituting m=n−k gives exactly 3≤m≤n−ℓ(n)−1. Small-n overlaps and the partition were also checked exactly.",
      "witness": "none",
      "search_method": "Uniform case-partition proof and exact integer boundary checks.",
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_v2_fixed_point_extension_v3_scratch/tcs_count_graphs_vc_at_most_k/audit/plain/attempt_4/audit_attempt4_checker.py"
    },
    {
      "idx": 5,
      "claim": "For every fixed k there is a polynomial-time exact algorithm. More explicitly, F(n,k) is computable in time at most poly(n)·sum_{t=0}^k binom(n,t)·2^{binom(t,2)+t}·[2(t+2)]^{2^t−1}.",
      "claim_sha256": "a1a82343d2cbfc3e60e579133f85193e3a3624e0ac7330ce099da54504123f95",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "For a cover C and I=V\\C, any alternative cover corresponds to removing an H-independent X⊆C and adding at least U_X. Hence C is minimum exactly when |U_X|≥|X| for every such X. At equality the alternative minimum cover is (C\\X)∪U_X, and the stated minimum-label condition is exactly the lexicographic tie-break. The capped-count/one-bit coordinates give the advertised finite state bound; summing over t, C, H, and neighborhood types yields the stated runtime and is polynomial for fixed k. Exhaustive testing over every graph through n=6 verified both the minimum and lex-first characterizations for every cover.",
      "witness": "none",
      "search_method": "Independent reconstruction of the cover-exchange bijection and DP, plus exhaustive exact testing.",
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_v2_fixed_point_extension_v3_scratch/tcs_count_graphs_vc_at_most_k/audit/plain/attempt_4/audit_attempt4_checker.py"
    },
    {
      "idx": 6,
      "claim": "Exact first- and second-moment formulas give certified bounds for all parameters. For 1≤m≤n, let q=N−binom(m,2), S1=binom(n,m)2^q, and S2=binom(n,m)·sum_{j=max(0,2m−n)}^m binom(m,j)binom(n−m,m−j)2^{N−2binom(m,2)+binom(j,2)}. Then max{2^q, ceil(S1²/S2)}≤F(n,n−m)≤min{2^N,S1}. In particular, q≤log₂F(n,n−m)≤q+n.",
      "claim_sha256": "639896230606d0a82488a3e98897ab46743ea8b6b12ed4cb855fca3930254430",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "With X(G) equal to the number of independent m-sets, direct double counting gives S1=Σ_G X(G). Ordered pairs intersecting in j vertices force exactly 2binom(m,2)−binom(j,2) absent edges, giving S2=Σ_G X(G)². The indicator bound and Cauchy–Schwarz yield the upper and second-moment lower bounds; fixing one independent m-set yields 2^q. Finally binom(n,m)≤2^n gives the logarithmic bracket. Exact enumeration through n=6 matched both moments and every bound.",
      "witness": "none",
      "search_method": "Independent double-counting and Cauchy–Schwarz proof with exhaustive exact-integer verification.",
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_v2_fixed_point_extension_v3_scratch/tcs_count_graphs_vc_at_most_k/audit/plain/attempt_4/audit_attempt4_checker.py"
    },
    {
      "idx": 7,
      "claim": "At the triangle-free endpoint, a substantial subclass is exactly countable in polynomial time. Let B_n be the number of labelled bipartite graphs and P_n=sum_{a=0}^n binom(n,a)2^{a(n−a)}. Then B_0=1 and B_n=(P_n−sum_{a=1}^{n−1}binom(n,a)B_aB_{n−a})/2. Hence F(n,n−3)≤2^N−B_n is an exact-arithmetic, polynomial-time computable bound.",
      "claim_sha256": "b2add0f9b562ae950d301750cdc32ff5d211579e88e07db9dd2face2df3ec7b2",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "P_n counts bipartite graphs with an ordered proper two-coloring. A bipartite graph with c connected components has exactly 2^c such colorings, so the labelled EGFs satisfy P(x)=B(x)^2. Coefficient extraction isolates the two endpoint convolution terms and gives the recurrence. Since bipartite graphs are triangle-free, B_n≤T(n,3), yielding the asserted upper bound on F. The recurrence reproduced the exhaustive counts through n=6.",
      "witness": "none",
      "search_method": "Independent labelled-component/EGF derivation and exhaustive exact enumeration.",
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_v2_fixed_point_extension_v3_scratch/tcs_count_graphs_vc_at_most_k/audit/plain/attempt_4/audit_attempt4_checker.py"
    },
    {
      "idx": 8,
      "claim": "Direct distinguished-vertex recurrence for the triangle-free endpoint. Let 𝒯_r be the set of labelled triangle-free graphs on [r], and let i(H) include the empty set in the number of independent vertex sets of H. Then T(0,3)=1 and, for n≥1, T(n,3)=sum_{d=0}^{n−1} binom(n−1,d)·sum_{H∈𝒯_{n−1−d}} i(H)^d. Equivalently, T(n,3)=nT(n−1,3)+sum_{d=2}^{n−1} binom(n−1,d)·sum_{H∈𝒯_{n−1−d}} i(H)^d.",
      "claim_sha256": "d4c98a3c34de88aced392ac5e6ece16e0423d635656dc7d2ec759aa7d0f5663e",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "After fixing a vertex v and its d-neighbor set S, triangle-freeness forces S independent. The residual graph H is triangle-free, and each s∈S independently chooses an independent neighborhood in H, producing i(H)^d reversible choices. The d=0 term is T(n−1,3), while Σ_{H∈𝒯_{n−2}}i(H)=T(n−1,3), so the d=1 term is (n−1)T(n−1,3). Both recurrences exactly reproduced all triangle-free counts through n=6.",
      "witness": "none",
      "search_method": "Independent reversible decomposition around a distinguished vertex and exhaustive exact verification.",
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_v2_fixed_point_extension_v3_scratch/tcs_count_graphs_vc_at_most_k/audit/plain/attempt_4/audit_attempt4_checker.py"
    },
    {
      "idx": 9,
      "claim": "The distinguished-vertex recurrence gives a deterministic exact algorithm for F(n,n−3) in time poly(n)·2^{binom(n−3,2)} with exponential space, or time poly(n)·2^{binom(n−2,2)} with polynomial space, for n≥3. Both exponents remain Θ(n²), so neither algorithm achieves the requested 2^{o(n²)} strength.",
      "claim_sha256": "842062d4adbf99357c9796619459e0fdf2c17b53665d25bfa3ca6ae59efbd58d",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "Only moments on r≤n−3 vertices occur after combining d=0,1. The subset-zeta construction correctly gives i(H)=g(complement E(H)) for every H in poly(r)·2^{binom(r,2)} time and space. Recomputing i(H) from its 2^r vertex subsets instead uses polynomial space and exponent binom(r,2)+r, maximized at r=n−3 as binom(n−2,2). Bottom-up smaller orders add only polynomial factors, and all integers have O(n²) bits. Exhaustive checking verified the zeta identity for every graph through r=5.",
      "witness": "none",
      "search_method": "Independent recurrence-dependency, zeta-transform, bit-complexity, and exponent analysis with exhaustive exact verification.",
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_v2_fixed_point_extension_v3_scratch/tcs_count_graphs_vc_at_most_k/audit/plain/attempt_4/audit_attempt4_checker.py"
    }
  ],
  "confirmed_refutations": [],
  "target_verdict": "VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS",
  "claimed_resolution_verdict": "ACCURATE",
  "target_evidence": "The draft does not prove the complete source target. It gives correct exact algorithms for k=o(n), fixed k, and trivial near-n endpoints, plus valid reductions, bounds, and Θ(n²)-exponent triangle-endpoint algorithms. It explicitly leaves the uniform strip ℓ(n)<k≤n−3 unresolved, including k=n−3, and therefore accurately claims only partial progress rather than a uniform 2^{o(n²)} algorithm.",
  "overall": "VERIFIED",
  "checks_performed": [
    "Read only /evidence/source.json and /evidence/parent.json as source material; used no web, retrieval database, treatment receipt, other arm, prior-run material, or other solution.",
    "Verified /evidence/parent.json SHA-256 exactly as 792af91d188a0bdf024c5c3d04409e91f6dc61d96b6e7498a2ef4183ae44c11a.",
    "Matched the mathematical object and quantifiers against the exact source target.",
    "Re-derived every bijection, extremal construction, recurrence, moment identity, parameter partition, and runtime/space exponent independently.",
    "Created and ran /work/audit_attempt4_checker.py (SHA-256 baec1d6cd0d7b4b7f1842f7ffe4856223bf7bc8d7d89fd402fdcb60ec34899d1).",
    "Exhaustively checked all labelled graphs on 0 through 6 vertices for the applicable endpoint identities, lower bounds, moment formulas, canonical-cover criteria, and bipartite and triangle-free recurrences.",
    "Checked the subset-zeta independent-set identity for every graph through order 5 and the runtime/strip algebra for n=2 through 128.",
    "The checker completed successfully and reported triangle-free counts [1,1,2,7,41,388,5789] and bipartite counts [1,1,2,7,41,376,5177]."
  ]
}
--- END AUDIT ---
